source.note: The shadow's hard-coded Saint John -> Quebec City transport argument, verbatim. The redesigned parameterized service must reproduce these numbers and verdict when fed these assumptions.

data.scenario: Saint John, NB -> Quebec City, QC — flight vs drive, 2 travelers, 5-day trip

roadDistanceKm.basis: ESTIMATED — road distance Saint John, NB to Quebec City via A-2/QC-85 corridor

driveHoursDoorToDoor.basis: ESTIMATED — owner framing: ~8h door to door with stops

fuelPricePerL.basis: ESTIMATED — CAD per litre, Oct 2026 Atlantic Canada

flightFarePerPerson.basis: ESTIMATED — CAD, one-stop YSJ->YQB economy, no direct flight exists

flightHoursDoorToDoor.basis: ESTIMATED — airport time + one connection + transfers

travelers.basis: scenario — the couple from the request

valueOfTimePerHourPerPerson.basis: ESTIMATED — guardian rate for scoring only, CAD

drive.case: Driving wins on money by $464 — but it spends 8 hours of the trip on the road, each way framing the arrival day as a write-off.

flight.case: Flying costs $464 more but buys back 2.5 hours and arrives with energy left — on a tight budget with a long trip ahead, the drive is the justifiable argue-back.

data.guardianRule: effective cost = all-in money + (hours x value-of-time x travelers); if effective costs are within 20%, BOTH options are emitted
data.verdict: drive scores better on effective cost

arrivalDayConsolidation.flight: land ~5.5h after leaving home -> transfer -> check-in -> only a gentle evening walk is honestly schedulable
arrivalDayConsolidation.drive: after 8h on the road the arrival day holds nothing but check-in and food — the plan must not pretend otherwise
